sale_conclusion: The selected sales place Walnut within a credible three-unit pricing range while illustrating why no single metric tells the full story. Atwood provides the closest Newhall location and an upper benchmark at $1,150,000, while Coronel provides the strongest rent-rule comparison at $1,090,000. Pinewood offers the closest physical comparison as three vintage residences on a large lot.

Santol and Harding establish lower reference points but carry meaningful differences in location, legal unit count, condition, and income basis. Price per unit and price per square foot should therefore be considered alongside each property's physical profile, occupancy, rent rules, and renovation level rather than read as stand-alone conclusions.
comparables_analysis.rent_conclusion: The selected monthly rents remain measured against the available survey. The $2,150 one-bedroom Pro Forma falls between the survey's 25th percentile and median, while the $2,400 two-bedroom Pro Forma remains below the 25th percentile. Atwood's achieved rents provide a directional cross-check but reflect materially superior condition.
comparables_analysis.integrated_conclusion: The six sales bracket Walnut's offering within the current small-property market, with the strongest support coming from Atwood's Newhall location, Coronel's comparable rent rules, and Pinewood's physical configuration. The rent survey supports a restrained Pro Forma rather than a top-of-market assumption. Buyers should evaluate the offering through the combined evidence and confirm leases, property condition, unit status, and operating assumptions during due diligence.

investment_overview: The LAAA Team of Marcus & Millichap is proud to present 24513–24519 Walnut Street, a three-unit residential investment in Old Town Newhall. Built in 1926 and 1954, the 2,364-square-foot property includes a duplex with two 2-bedroom/1-bath residences and a detached 1-bedroom/1-bath rear home on a 9,379-square-foot COR-zoned lot.

The investment offers 21.9% gross rent upside from reported monthly rents of $5,700 to broker pro forma of $6,950. The two duplex residences each generate $1,800 per month against a $2,400 pro forma, while the rear home generates $2,100 against a $2,150 pro forma. The three residences are fully occupied, subject to lease verification.

Newhall Metrolink Station is approximately 0.26 mile from the property, and Old Town Newhall’s Main Street district provides nearby dining, arts, library, and civic amenities. The lot’s alley access and COR zoning support independent ADU and site-planning study, with no entitlement represented. The offering is positioned for small-property investors, 1031 exchange buyers, and owner-operators seeking occupied income with defined rent upside.
location_overview: Old Town Newhall combines Main Street dining, arts, and civic amenities within a compact historic district. The Old Town Newhall Library is approximately 0.09 mile from Walnut Street, The MAIN performance venue is 0.30 mile away, and William S. Hart Park is approximately 0.46 mile south.

Newhall Metrolink Station is approximately 0.26 mile from the property and serves the Antelope Valley Line, with 324 parking spaces listed by Metrolink. Interstate 5 access is approximately one mile west, and Henry Mayo Newhall Hospital is approximately 1.71 miles away.

Santa Clarita’s 2024 population estimate was 229,159. Census data reports median household income of $123,062, median gross rent of $2,544, and a 34.1-minute mean commute for 2020–2024. College of the Canyons reports 40,987 annual enrollment, adding a major education and employment anchor in the valley.
